open_points.subject: sandbox environment own_proc
open_points.text: The formal invariant adds `own_proc` to `environment = {python_stdlib_runtime, code, inputs, exchange_dir, own_proc}`, while rule 1 still describes an environment holding only the runtime and exchange directory and never defines `own_proc`, its mount point, contents, permissions or visibility to function code.
open_points.question: What exactly is `own_proc`, and which process information must a function be able to observe through it?
options: Mount a private procfs at `/proc` for the execution's PID namespace
Expose only a specified subset of process information
Treat `own_proc` as an internal sandbox property with no filesystem-visible procfs
open_points.default_guess: Mount a private procfs at `/proc`, read-only from the function's perspective.

witness.initial: A contract has one integer output, a trial case without expected outputs, and an implementation whose `run` catches errors from `os.stat('/proc/self')` and returns whether that path exists.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel admits it and activates it.
outcomes: An implementation that mounts private procfs returns true.
An implementation that treats `own_proc` as non-filesystem sandbox metadata returns false.
witness.observer: The run caller and trace reader see different output digests.

open_points.subject: K-02 function purity and access to time or chance
open_points.text: The changed K-02 says code that gets time or chance some other way "is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other", while State 0 defines a node as a "pure function", excludes any "stateful" function, and requires "no clock, no randomness"; A03 is still titled "without a clock".
open_points.question: Are functions allowed to produce output dependent on an untrapped source of time or chance, or must the purity/no-clock/no-randomness rule still cause such an execution or implementation to be refused?
options: Allow it and judge only the particular observed outputs
Refuse every detected dependency and require the isolation boundary to prevent all others
Treat nondeterministic output itself as a failure even when no trap was recorded
open_points.default_guess: Follow the changed detailed rule: allow untrapped dependencies and judge only the observed output.

witness.initial: A contract has one integer output, and its corpus contains a case with no expected output.
events: An authoring agent submits code returning an integer derived from `id(object())`, an untrapped process-dependent value.
Admission observes a schema-valid integer and activates the implementation.
Two callers run the active flow with equal inputs in separate fresh sandbox processes.
outcomes: Under the changed K-02 rule, both executions may succeed with different output digests because no listed trap was hit.
Under the pure/no-clock/no-randomness rules, the implementation or execution must be refused or the equal-input outputs must not differ.
witness.observer: The callers and trace readers see either two successful differing outputs or a refusal/non-varying result.

open_points.subject: admission reuse and the repaired-slot guarantee
open_points.text: K-05 says a failed real execution can be captured "so a repaired slot stays repaired", but A04 admits from one set of observations and reuses the recorded verdict forever for the same implementation and corpus digest, while changed K-02 permits untrapped time- or chance-dependent behavior.
open_points.question: Does passing a captured case once permanently satisfy the repaired-slot guarantee, or must the kernel prevent an admitted implementation from later producing an output that fails that same case?
options: A recorded passing observation is sufficient; "stays repaired" is not a runtime invariant
Admission must reject or detect implementations whose result can vary for a case
The captured corpus must be rechecked before activation or real execution
open_points.default_guess: Treat the recorded verdict as authoritative and regard "stays repaired" as only a corpus/admission-process claim.

witness.initial: A failed execution has been captured as a trial case whose expected integer output is 0; the serving implementation still serves until another is activated.
events: An agent submits a replacement whose schema-valid output is `id(object()) & 1`.
Its admission execution happens to return 0, so A04 records `admitted` and activates it.
A real run of the same input in a fresh sandbox returns 1.
The agent submits the equal implementation again under the unchanged corpus digest.
outcomes: A04 and M08 reuse the admitted verdict, keep the implementation active, and the real run exposes output 1.
The promise that the repaired slot stays repaired requires the implementation not to serve an output that fails the captured case, so activation or execution must instead be prevented or revalidated.
witness.observer: The run caller sees either the schema-valid but regression-producing value 1 or a prevention/refusal.
